title: Bulk Loading with COPY & \copy
description: Import and export millions of rows per second using binary/CSV streams with COPY and client-side \copy.

data.text: When loading millions of rows, executing individual `INSERT` statements (even in batches) has severe query parsing and transaction overhead. The **`COPY`** command streams raw data directly into the database engine, bypassing query planning and achieving ingestion rates exceeding 100,000+ rows per second.

data.title: Streaming CSV Bulk Load with Options
data.content: Configuring header skip, delimiter, and NULL string representations.
data.code:
-- High-performance client-side CSV load
\copy measurements (sensor_id, temperature, recorded_at) 
FROM 'readings_2024.csv' 
WITH (
    FORMAT csv, 
    HEADER true, 
    DELIMITER ',', 
    NULL 'NA'
);

data.title: COPY on the server, \copy from your laptop
data.content: `COPY` runs inside the database process and reads a file on the server. The psql meta-command `\copy` streams a local file over the connection, so it works without server filesystem access.
data.code:
-- Server-side: the file must be readable by the postgres process
COPY orders (id, customer_id, amount, ordered_at)
FROM '/var/lib/postgresql/data/orders.csv'
WITH (FORMAT csv, HEADER true, DELIMITER ',', NULL '');

-- Client-side (psql meta-command): streams a local file
\copy orders (id, customer_id, amount, ordered_at) \
    FROM 'orders.csv' WITH (FORMAT csv, HEADER true)

data.title: A repeatable bulk-load recipe
data.text: Load into an UNLOGGED staging table, run `ANALYZE` on it, then `INSERT ... SELECT` into the real table inside one transaction and `ANALYZE` the target afterward. Consider dropping non-critical indexes and disabling triggers during a very large one-off load, then rebuilding. Raising `maintenance_work_mem` and setting `synchronous_commit = off` for the load session is usually safe because a crash just means reloading.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `COPY` is the fastest method for bulk inserting data into PostgreSQL.
Use `\copy` in `psql` to load files directly from your local development machine.
Temporarily dropping indexes and foreign keys before bulk loading can increase ingestion speed by 5x to 10x.
